how: S3, one steady move. The dive blends the hold's own track into the close side's own track, the rise the close side's track into the travel's, in coordinates about the eye of the storm (log of height, arc and azimuth of the point under the camera, orientation against a look at the eye, field of view). The weight is a trapezoid of rate: rampIn and rampOut are the shares of the segment over which the rate rises from the first track's and falls to the last track's. at is the share of the segment where the side changes (T). arc is the power of that weight by which the arc from the eye changes (1 is even): above 1 the camera stays over the storm while it is low and swings out late, so the ground in frame stays inside the plates of the place while they are needed (G13).

ring.how: The grain of the ring in the dive and the rise. The grain is a picture of round specks on the ring plane; from near they are short strokes across the ring's circles. along: share of a full turn over which the grain is averaged along the ring's own circles, so a speck becomes a piece of an arc. The width is full below the first height of near and none from the second on, which is the grain the travel after the rise is drawn with.

near.how: Camera heights in radii between which the looks of the dive and the rise that the travel does not have go away: whole below the first, none from the second on (the rise ends at 4.196, so its last frames are drawn as the travel is).

rim.how: The air at the limb in the dive and the rise. line and layers: for the line shell and the three layers of haze.json the values that take the place of away there (cosine to the Sun where the light begins, where it is whole, gain): the line weaker and the light falling over a wider span of the limb, so the rim is a falloff that tapers into the night side. dim: how much of the sky behind the air goes for each unit of its optical depth, so a star at the bright edge is dimmed. All of it by the weight of near, and by the share the view is away from the hold's.

sky.how: turnFrame: the first frame of the dive that is drawn with the sky turned to the sky of the close view; every frame before it keeps the sky of the hold. The engine's own law turns the sky from the first frame of the dive to the handover, about 113 degrees in all. The plate of the hold carries the approved picture's flare around the Sun and the Sun stays where the light comes from, so that turn drew the flare away from the Sun (two stars at 4688 and 4696) and by 4707 it had brought the film's warm band to the limb. Here the sky stays with the Sun until the Sun has set behind the limb (4709) and the globe fills the frame but for the upper right corner: at 4722 that corner reaches 1.1 degrees past the limb (40 px), at 4723 0.8, and from 4723 to 4730 only the glow of the air is seen in it (assets-src/neptune/place/skyin.ts prints the corner per frame). The turn is whole long before the sky of the close view fades in (24 frames before the handover at 4758), so that sky no longer swings into place. The rise keeps the engine's law.
